approachAdjustment: Do not wire a Temporal client into quarry-control (it is a stubbed schedule client). Follow the repo reconciler pattern: edge route to control job record desired_state (cancel, pause, resume via the existing PUT /v1/jobs/{id}) to orchestrator jobs.Manager, which already holds the client, sends the signal; add control-signal handlers to BatchJobWF or document batch as non-cancellable. Build /errors from existing page_failed and page_blocked events, and implement the live tail in the edge handler by polling control with after_seq (no new bus). Treat paginated result data as a separate sub-item: crawl output is not stored per job today (events carry excerpts only; pages go to artifacts or Data Plane when ingest is on), so a result source must be decided first.
effortNote: Raised from M: lifecycle routes (status, cancel, pause, resume, errors, ongoing, tail) are M, but result pagination, run origin and stage timeline add a data-source decision and push the total to L.
verdictReason: The gap is confirmed and the Temporal handlers do exist for crawl, but the item places the Temporal client in the wrong service, overlooks that batch has no signal handlers, and treats result pagination as route wiring when no per-job result store exists.
